description_full: Bachem Holding AG, together with its subsidiaries, provides products for research, clinical development, and commercial application to pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies worldwide. It engages in the development, production, and regulatory support of peptide active pharmaceutical ingredients, such as peptide and oligonucleotide new chemical entities (NCEs). The company also offers commercial NCEs and generics; and project management, quality and regulatory, analytical, good manufacturing practice production, research grade production, and supply and vertical integration services. Bachem Holding AG was incorporated in 1971 and is headquartered in Bubendorf, Switzerland. Bachem Holding AG operates as a subsidiary of Ingro Finanz AG.

financial_summary: Bachem Holding AG is a mid-cap healthcare business with a $7.1B market cap on $848M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +15% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.
Returns on capital run at 12% against a 8% cost of capital, a 4-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it, with gross margins sitting at 30%.
The company is burning through $71M of cash, and without positive owner earnings any valuation rests on hope rather than evidence.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year.

Shareholder yield is only 0.6%, a thin return of capital, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome, and within its sector the business captures 2.7× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
